questions.question: What did Descartes formulate by the time he exited the room after his three dreams on the night of 10â11 November 1619?
options: analytic geometry and the idea of applying the mathematical method to philosophy
a new system of military engineering
the Cartesian coordinate system
a treatise on the passions of the soul
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that by the time he exited the room, Descartes had formulated analytic geometry and the idea of applying the mathematical method to philosophy.
Incorrect. The article does not state that he formulated a new system of military engineering during that night.
Incorrect. While the Cartesian coordinate system is named after him, the article does not say he formulated it during that night in Neuburg an der Donau.
Incorrect. The Passions of the Soul was published much later, in 1649, not formulated during that night.

questions.question: Which work did Descartes dedicate to Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia?
options: Principia Philosophiae
Meditations on First Philosophy
Discourse on the Method
The World
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Principia Philosophiae was dedicated to Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia.
Incorrect. Meditations on First Philosophy was written in Latin and addressed to the learned, not dedicated to Princess Elisabeth.
Incorrect. The Discourse on the Method was published in 1637 as an introduction to three essays, not dedicated to Princess Elisabeth.
Incorrect. The World was a work Descartes abandoned plans to publish in 1633 after Galileo's condemnation; it is not described as dedicated to Princess Elisabeth.

questions.question: What did Descartes publish in 1637?
options: parts of Treatise on the World in three essays preceded by Discourse on the Method
Meditations on First Philosophy
Principles of Philosophy
The Passions of the Soul

questions.question: What was Descartes's best-known philosophical statement?
options: cogito, ergo sum
I think, therefore I am not
existence precedes essence
the unexamined life is not worth living
answer_explanations: Correct. The article identifies 'cogito, ergo sum' ('I think, therefore I am') as Descartes's best-known philosophical statement.
Incorrect. 'I think, therefore I am not' contradicts the statement given in the article.
Incorrect. 'Existence precedes essence' is associated with existentialism, not with Descartes in this article.
Incorrect. 'The unexamined life is not worth living' is associated with Socrates, not Descartes.

questions.question: Why did Descartes abandon plans to publish Treatise on the World?
options: because Galileo was condemned by the Italian Inquisition in 1633
because he moved to Sweden in 1649
because Princess Elisabeth urged him to write a different philosophy
because the University of Utrecht condemned Cartesian philosophy in 1643
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in 1633, Galileo was condemned by the Italian Inquisition, and Descartes abandoned plans to publish Treatise on the World.
Incorrect. Descartes moved to Sweden in 1649, well after he had already abandoned Treatise on the World.
Incorrect. Cardinal BÃ©rulle urged Descartes to write an exposition of his new philosophy, but this was not the reason he abandoned Treatise on the World.
Incorrect. The University of Utrecht condemned Cartesian philosophy in 1643, which was after Descartes had already abandoned Treatise on the World.

questions.question: What did Descartes do during the siege of La Rochelle in 1627?
options: he observed the siege and studied the physical properties of Richelieu's dike mathematically
he commanded the French forces
he published Discourse on the Method
he met Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Descartes was present at the siege of La Rochelle as an observer and studied mathematically everything he saw, including the physical properties of the great dike Richelieu was building.
Incorrect. Descartes was an observer at the siege, not a commander of French forces.
Incorrect. Discourse on the Method was published in 1637, not during the 1627 siege.
Incorrect. Descartes met Princess Elisabeth of Bohemia later; their correspondence began between 1643 and 1649.

questions.question: What did Descartes identify as a fifth, better and more secure source of wisdom in the preface to the French edition of Principles of Philosophy?
options: the search for first causes
the study of military engineering
the reading of ancient Greek literature
the avoidance of all passions
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in the preface to the French edition, Descartes identified four ordinary sources of wisdom and finally said there is a fifth, better and more secure, consisting in the search for first causes.
Incorrect. Military engineering was something Descartes studied in Breda, not a source of wisdom mentioned in the preface.
Incorrect. Ancient Greek literature was a passion of Queen Christina, not a source of wisdom identified by Descartes in the preface.
Incorrect. Descartes did not deprecate the passions and did not identify their avoidance as the fifth source of wisdom.

questions.question: What did Descartes and Pierre Chanut make observations with in Stockholm?
options: a Torricellian mercury barometer
a telescope
a microscope
a pendulum clock
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Chanut and Descartes made observations with a Torricellian mercury barometer in Stockholm.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Descartes using a telescope with Chanut.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Descartes using a microscope with Chanut.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Descartes using a pendulum clock with Chanut.

questions.question: What did Descartes conclude from the dreams he had on the night of 10â11 November 1619?
options: that the pursuit of science would be the pursuit of true wisdom and a central part of his life's work
that he should become a lawyer
that he should join the Dutch States Army
that he should publish Treatise on the World immediately
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Descartes concluded from these dreams that the pursuit of science would prove to be, for him, the pursuit of true wisdom and a central part of his life's work.
Incorrect. Studying law was his father's wish, not a conclusion from the dreams.
Incorrect. Descartes joined the Dutch States Army in 1618, before the dreams of November 1619.
Incorrect. Descartes eventually abandoned plans to publish Treatise on the World; he did not conclude from the dreams that he should publish it immediately.
